analysis.summary: Runway, Pika and Luma are all moving into ChatGPT and Claude. Runway ships the most model pages, but Pika is out-teaching it with prompt guides.

points.text: Runway updated 27 older pages, mostly pages for other companies' models like Kling, Veo and Wan. That points to a refresh push to stay current.
Pika published 11 how-to pages this month, mostly prompt guides for models like Seedance 2.5 and Wan 3.0. Runway has 7 how-tos in total.
HeyGen wrote industry pages for travel, real estate and finance, plus 5 case studies. Runway has 2 case studies and no industry pages in this data.

gaps.title: Filmmaker workflow guides
gaps.text: Pika's guides cover prompts and ads. Runway has only one previs (pre-shoot planning) how-to. Step-by-step pages for film and production teams are open.

gaps.title: Industry pages for film and ads
gaps.text: HeyGen builds pages for many industries. No one here does this for commercials, studios, or commerce teams, so Runway could own those searches.

gaps.title: Customer stories from production teams
gaps.text: Runway has 2 case studies and HeyGen has 5, all in non-film fields. Real studio and ad-agency results are open for evaluators.

versus.Pika: Pika puts its energy into teaching and prompt guides. Runway puts more into model, product and plugin landing pages.
versus.Luma AI: Luma publishes far less, only 3 new pages. Runway's 21 new pages cover far more topics, including research and app launches.
versus.Kling AI: No pages appear in the data, so no comparison is possible. Runway still hosts Kling 3.0, O3 and 4.0 pages.
versus.Seedance: Seedance has thousands of templated pages but no activity this month. Runway publishes fewer pages but keeps them fresh. It also hosts Seedance 2.0 and 2.5 pages.
versus.HeyGen: HeyGen writes for industries and customer stories. Runway writes for model fans and developers, with fewer case studies and no industry pages.
